title: How this lesson works
text: LAB Before you start · your group ≈ 2 min How this lesson works Slideshow lead Reads each slide aloud and moves the deck forward. Whiteboard scribe Holds the dry erase marker and works problems at the whiteboard. Timekeeper · support Starts each timer and keeps the group on pace. Checker · support Asks "How do we know?" before anyone presses Show answer. Explicit instruction Read it together. Then one person restates it in their own words. Check your understanding Solve alone, compare answers, agree — then press Show answer. Group tasks Start the timer. Everyone contributes before you move on. Exit ticket On your own. Submit it with this lesson's assignment. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 02 / 32 2 students: lead + timekeeper, scribe + checker. 3 students: third person takes both support duties. Roles rotate at each discussion. Everyone submits their own work.

title: Lab briefing
text: LAB Lab briefing · before you touch anything ≈ 3 min Today is a lab. Equipment lead Sets up, runs, and puts away the sensor. Data recorder Logs every trial — raw numbers, units, notes. Analyst Finds slopes and averages; checks the math. Safety lead Clears the space and calls "stop" if needed. 01 Predict before every measurement — write it down first. 02 Record raw data, not just the final answer. 03 Repeat — one trial is not evidence. 04 No equipment? Ask your teacher for a simulation or sample data set. Equipment check Vernier motion detectors (1 per 4–5 students) Laptops with Logger Pro or Graphical Analysis Target graphs (projected or printed) Whiteboards for sketching Exit ticket slips Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 03 / 32

title: Lab setup
text: LAB Lab setup · step by step ≈ 5 min Set up the Walk the Line lab 01 Put the motion detector on a table at the end of a clear 4 m lane, aimed straight down it. 02 Connect it to the laptop. Open Graphical Analysis and show position vs. time . 03 Tape the floor at 0.5 m, then every 0.5 m out to 3.5 m. 04 Start at a distance your teacher approves for this detector. Check its minimum range first. 05 Click Collect , then walk to match the target graph. SETUP DIAGRAM · not to scale Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 04 / 32

title: Setup check
text: LAB Setup check · before trial 1 ≈ 2 min Does your setup work? Stand still at 1.0 m A flat line at 1.0 m. Walk slowly away A line that rises steadily. Readings jump around? Aim the detector at your chest; clear the lane. All three pass? Start real trials. If one fails, fix it first — bad setup means bad data. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 05 / 32

title: The asteroid thread
text: LAB The asteroid thread What we know so far We have position data for 2026-XJ — but we need to talk about how it changes over time. Today Velocity is HOW position changes with time. Our fictional model includes 2026-XJ's velocity — today we learn what velocity actually means. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 07 / 32

title: Same time, different travel
text: LAB See it → describe it Target S1 Same time, different travel Compare how far A and B move in 2 seconds. Which has the greater speed? A steeper line A B Both move right. B travels farther in the same time. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 10 / 32

title: Same trip, different rates
text: LAB Check your understanding Target S1 Same trip, different rates Two walkers each move +12 m. Walker A takes 6 s and Walker B takes 4 s. Who has the greater average velocity? Show the comparison. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Your turn Work it out on paper. Then press Show answer to check. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 11 / 32

title: Same displacement, different velocity
text: 2026-XJ · The Line Moves · Graphic novel, page 9 Same displacement, different velocity Maz and Eli each walk six meters east. Maz takes six seconds and Eli takes twelve. Maz averages one meter per second east; Eli averages half a meter per second east. Both walkers reach the same endpoint. Their elapsed times differ. Why does the same displacement produce different average velocities? Part 1 · Compare your motion predictions · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 3

title: Read a graph as a motion story
text: LAB See it → describe it Target S1 Read a graph as a motion story Rising: position increases. Flat: position stays the same. Falling: position decreases. Position over time Move right, stop, then move left. The graph is not a hill. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 13 / 32

title: Speed and velocity
text: LAB Definitions ≈ 10 min Speed and velocity Speed · scalar speed = distance ÷ time Velocity · vector v = Δx ÷ Δt Physics unit m/s Explain both definitions in your own words. Then compare units with your partner. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 14 / 32

title: Convert the asteroid's speed
text: LAB How fast is 2026-XJ? ≈ 10 min Convert the asteroid's speed Fictional model ≈ 8,500 m/s In km/h ≈ 30,600 km/h In mph ≈ 19,000 mph Way faster than any car or commercial plane. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 15 / 32

title: Average velocity and average speed
text: LAB Explicit instruction Target S1 Average velocity and average speed v̄ = Δx / Δt Average speed = total distance / elapsed time Average velocity carries direction. Average speed describes path length covered per second. An instantaneous velocity describes a particular moment. An average summarizes an interval. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 16 / 32

title: Find a rate in two steps
text: LAB I do · divide once Target S1 Find a rate in two steps The cart moves +6 m in 3 s. Share the change equally among the seconds. +6 ÷ 3 = +2 m/s Two meters each second Each second contributes the same change. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 17 / 32

title: Round-trip rates
text: LAB Check your understanding Target S1 Round-trip rates A student walks 6 m east and 6 m west in 8 s total. Find average speed and average velocity. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Your turn Work it out on paper. Then press Show answer to check. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 18 / 32

title: A round trip still includes motion
text: 2026-XJ · The Line Moves · Graphic novel, page 10 A round trip still includes motion The notebook shows six meters east and six west in twelve seconds. Average speed is one meter per second and average velocity is zero. The route has 12 m of distance and zero displacement over 12 s. Which measurements would reveal the motion that the zero average velocity hides? Part 2 · Collect and check your trials · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 3

title: Walk the line.

title: The sign gives the direction
text: LAB See it → describe it Target S1 Lab The sign gives the direction Right is positive. +2 m/s means 2 m each second right. −2 m/s means 2 m each second left. Same speed, opposite directions Speed is the size. Velocity also includes direction. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 21 / 32

title: Position is the graph’s height; velocity
text: LAB Explicit instruction Target S1 Lab Position is the graph’s height; velocity is its slope Position–time segment Motion Straight, rising line Constant positive velocity Horizontal line Position stays constant, v = 0 Straight, falling line Constant negative velocity Curve with changing slope Velocity changes Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 22 / 32

title: What does a position–time graph tell us?
text: LAB Group discussion ≈ 13 min What does a position–time graph tell us? Group protocol 1 · Think alone for a minute · 2 · Go around — everyone shares · 3 · Scribe shows the reasoning at the whiteboard; everyone writes their own answer Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 23 / 32

title: Slope of a p–t graph = velocity
text: LAB Reading the slope ≈ 13 min Slope of a p–t graph = velocity Steeper Faster. Flat Not moving — position isn't changing. Negative slope Moving in the − direction. here: toward the sensor Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 24 / 32

title: Walk the graph, then explain it
text: 2026-XJ · The Line Moves · Graphic novel, page 11 Walk the graph, then explain it A position–time graph joins zero seconds and one meter, four seconds and five meters, six seconds and five meters, then ten seconds and one meter. The rising, flat and falling segments tell different parts of the trip. How can +1, 0 and −1 m/s describe the segments while the whole-trip average is zero? Part 3 · Defend the whole motion story · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 3

title: Velocity in the fictional model
text: LAB Back to 2026-XJ ≈ 13 min Our fictional model uses position–time data. A slope gives velocity along the plotted axis; a full trajectory needs all relevant directions. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 26 / 32

title: Read the endpoints
text: LAB Try it as a group Target S1 Read the endpoints At 0 s: 2 m. At 2 s: 6 m. First find the position change. Then divide by 2 s. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. title: Match the graph investigation
text: LAB Investigation 1.1 Target S1 Match the graph investigation • Clear a walking lane and follow the detector’s minimum-distance guidance. • Start about 1 m from the detector. Predict a graph for walking away steadily. • Record a safe walking trial. Repeat for standing still and walking toward it. • For each trial, sketch the graph and calculate one slope. • Submit three labeled graphs and one sentence connecting slope to motion. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 28 / 32

title: Does a high line mean fast?
text: LAB Try it as a group Target S1 Does a high line mean fast? This cart stays at 8 m for 4 seconds. Is it moving? Explain using the graph. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Position over time The height is position. The slope describes velocity. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 29 / 32

title: Your turn: return toward zero
text: LAB Try it yourself Target S1 Your turn: return toward zero A cart goes from 8 m to 2 m in 3 s. Find its velocity. Right is positive. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Position over time The position decreases. Lab · Day 3 · Velocity Antocci Physics · 30 / 32

title: Explain the slope
text: LAB Put it in words Target S1 Explain the slope The line ___, so the position ___. The velocity is ___ because the change is ___ in ___ seconds. A path through the problem 01 Read Two positions and two times. 02 Change Finish minus start. 03 Share Change divided by time. Read one step at a time.
